{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to qualify as an eligible employee.",
        "context_quotes": ["F000"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F002:F004",
        "choice_text": "All three criteria must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees who work outside the U.S.)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "need not be",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the counting of prior employment periods complies with the rules governing breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not be counted",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F007"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee had a break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be counted",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F008:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301"],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for furthering education or for childrearing purposes)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F008"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer when the employee has been absent due to USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be also counted",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": ["USERRA"],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002", "F010"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months and the employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002", "F010"],
        "scope_text": "For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002", "F011"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002", "F011"],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must do so uniformly",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F003", "F012"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785); the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, and the determination is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all hours worked or in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F003", "F012"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may be used",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F003", "F013"],
        "scope_text": "In determining an employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave when returning or reemployed following USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall be credited",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave; accordingly, a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has the hours that would have been worked added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally be used",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA"],
        "statement": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be able to clearly demonstrate",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (such as full-time teachers defined in § 825.102 who often work outside the classroom or at home) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001:F003", "F015"],
        "scope_text": "In making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be made",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may be",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave (referencing § 825.300(b) for rules governing eligibility notices)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F004", "F016"],
        "scope_text": "To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to that notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite, for that specific notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may not terminate",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer employs 50 or more employees at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, but expects the employee count to drop below 50 before the leave begins.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must grant",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when the 50-employee threshold is met, even if the employer expects that the number of employees will drop below 50 before the leave is scheduled to begin (for example, employing 60 employees in August when notice is given for leave to begin in December when the employee count is expected to drop to 40)."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to qualify as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three criteria must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees who work outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the counting of prior employment periods complies with the rules governing breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee had a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for furthering education or for childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer when the employee has been absent due to USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months and the employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785); the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, and the determination is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all hours worked or in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining an employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave when returning or reemployed following USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave; accordingly, a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has the hours that would have been worked added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541).
unit_attributes.modality_quote: must be able to clearly demonstrate
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee (such as full-time teachers defined in § 825.102 who often work outside the classroom or at home) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave (referencing § 825.300(b) for rules governing eligibility notices).

unit_attributes.scope_text: To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to that notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite, for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer employs 50 or more employees at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, but expects the employee count to drop below 50 before the leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when the 50-employee threshold is met, even if the employer expects that the number of employees will drop below 50 before the leave is scheduled to begin (for example, employing 60 employees in August when notice is given for leave to begin in December when the employee count is expected to drop to 40).
